migrates_from._note: One-time MOVE into ~/.my-llm-wiki on first launch of the rebuilt app (desktop paths::migrate_legacy). No symlink, no fallback reads — a clean cutover, so any leftover reference to these fails loudly.

capture_toolchain._note: Single machine-readable catalog for capture capability profiles, tool probes, install commands, and mainland-China variants. Skills declare profile ids in registry/skills.json; preflight.py evaluates only the requested profiles. Tool installation is always opt-in.

mcp._note: Single source of truth for Browser MCP registration across hosts (parallel to default_skill_targets). The Browser serves MCP at {endpoint} behind the same Bearer token as /api/v1. Registration recipes are each host's OWN `mcp add` command — install-browser.py proposes them after install and runs one only with explicit per-host consent (never edits a host config file directly); doctor.py reports 'Browser installed but host X unregistered' and stale entries. MCP is an access form, not the capability itself: hosts without MCP reach the same backend through wiki_ops.py browser-search / local-search / read-pages, fully equivalent.

claude.register_command: claude mcp add --scope user --transport http my-llm-wiki {endpoint} --header "Authorization: Bearer {token}"

codex.register_note: Codex reads the bearer token from $LLM_WIKI_WEB_TOKEN — export LLM_WIKI_WEB_TOKEN="$(cat ~/.my-llm-wiki/connector/token)" in the profile Codex runs from.

agents.register_note: No MCP registration CLI known for this host — use the equivalent CLI fallback (wiki_ops.py browser-search / local-search / read-pages).

workbuddy.register_note: No MCP registration CLI known for this host — use the equivalent CLI fallback (wiki_ops.py browser-search / local-search / read-pages).

first_run._note: Browser port is resolved like the app itself (desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs): port_pref_file > $PORT > default_port. Health probe only needs liveness — an auth-gated response (token required) still proves the server is up.
